memos.headline: AAPL and JPM Lead at 52-Week Highs; GOOGL Breaks Down to Oversold Territory
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe today. AAPL sits just 0.2% off its 52-week high with +21% over four weeks and massive relative strength vs SPY of +20.4% over that period — this is the strongest momentum name in the group, though RSI at 65 and an 8.7% premium to the 50-day mean suggest a near-term pause is possible. JPM is literally printing a new 52-week high with RSI 68.2 and consistent relative strength across timeframes (+4.8% 4w, +9.6% 12w vs SPY), making it the cleanest trend-following long here. On the other side, GOOGL is deeply oversold at RSI 32.5, down 12.3% below its 50-day mean and 20.6% off its high — this looks like a falling knife rather than a buy-the-dip setup given negative relative strength across all windows. CAT's 4-week -15.9% plunge despite a strong 26-week return of +37.3% signals a potential trend reversal; I'd need to see it reclaim its 50-day mean before getting involved.

views.note: Dominant relative strength (+20.4% vs SPY over 4w) and sitting 0.2% from 52w high; would reassess on a close below the 50-day mean (~306).
New 52-week high with low ATR (2.14%), strong trend above both moving averages, and positive relative strength across all timeframes; invalidated below 335.
Healthy uptrend with +22.6% above 200d mean and only 3.6% off highs, but flat 4-week relative strength tempers conviction; watch 405 support.
Strong 4-week move (+14.1%) but RSI at 72.1 is the most overbought in the universe, suggesting mean-reversion risk near-term; would buy a pullback to the 50-day area (~147).

Middling RSI 51.1 and flat positioning near the 50d mean; no clear directional edge — would go long above 215 or step aside below 195.

memos.headline: NVDA and GOOGL Post Extraordinary Earnings Growth; XOM and UNH Show Cash-Flow Compression
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe between names with accelerating earnings power and those facing margin headwinds. NVDA's 2027Q1 delivered $81.6B in revenue (+85% YoY) with a staggering 71.5% net margin and net income up 211% YoY on just $8.5B of total debt — this is the cleanest earnings story in the group. GOOGL's freshly filed 2026Q2 shows $119.8B revenue (+24% YoY) and a 93.7% net margin producing $112.2B of net income, though I flag that margin level as likely inflated by a one-time gain and would need the 10-Q detail to sustain conviction. On the other side, XOM's net income collapsed 46% YoY to $4.2B on a 4.9% net margin, and UNH grew revenue only 2% with flat earnings — both signal durable earnings compression until commodity or medical-cost trends reverse. MSFT and AMZN remain solid double-digit growers with expanding margins, while CAT's 22% revenue growth and 27% earnings growth on cyclical strength deserve attention but carry cycle risk.

views.note: Revenue +85% YoY, net margin 71.5%, net income +211% YoY on minimal debt — the most powerful earnings trajectory in the universe.
Revenue +24% YoY and $112B net income are impressive, but the 93.7% net margin likely includes a large non-recurring item; I need the full 10-Q breakdown to raise confidence.
Revenue +18% YoY, net margin 38.3%, net income +23% YoY with moderate $40B debt — durable cloud-driven earnings expansion.
Revenue +17% YoY with net income surging 77% to $30.3B and margin expanding to 16.7%, though $123B total debt warrants monitoring.
Solid +17% revenue growth and 26.6% net margin, but $82.7B debt load and slower earnings growth vs peers keep me neutral.
Revenue +22% and earnings +27% YoY are strong, but cyclical exposure and $36B debt against $17B quarterly revenue introduce downside risk if orders slow.
Steady 10% revenue growth and 33% net margin are respectable for a bank, but $449B total debt and single-digit earnings growth limit upside conviction.
Net income down 46% YoY to $4.2B on a 4.9% net margin signals severe earnings compression; I would revisit only if margins recover above 8%.
Revenue growth of just 2% and flat net income on $78B of debt point to stalling earnings power; medical cost ratio improvement would change my view.
Modest 7% revenue growth and 18.5% net margin are stable but unexciting; earnings growth of only 4% doesn't justify a premium.

memos.headline: Fed on Pause but Sticky 3.5% CPI and Rising Long Rates Squeeze Duration and Favor Defensives Over Cyclicals
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly on pause—upper bound at 3.75% unchanged over three months after 75 bps of cuts over the past year—while headline CPI is running at 3.5% y/y, well above target and likely keeping the FOMC sidelined through at least September. The labor market is stable with unemployment at 4.2%, down 10 bps over three months, which removes any urgency to ease further. What concerns me most is the long end: the 10y yield has surged 38 bps in three months to 4.69%, and the 10y-2y spread has compressed 17 bps to just 0.34 pp, signaling the market is repricing term premium higher on persistent inflation. This is a headwind for duration-sensitive growth names and a mixed bag for banks (higher long rates help NIM but curve flattening offsets). A CPI print falling below 3% or unemployment breaking above 4.5% would change my regime call from 'pause with hawkish tilt' to 'easing imminent.'

views.note: Rising long-end yields at 4.69% pressure high-multiple growth, but stable consumer spending from low unemployment provides a floor.
Duration-sensitive valuation faces headwinds from the 38 bps 3-month rise in the 10y, though paused Fed limits further front-end damage.
Highest-duration name in the universe is most vulnerable to the 10y at 4.69% and sticky 3.5% CPI keeping the Fed on hold.
Higher absolute long rates support NIM expansion, and a 4.2% unemployment rate keeps credit quality intact, though curve flattening tempers conviction.
Stable labor market supports demand, but the pause regime and sticky inflation create an ambiguous macro backdrop for energy cyclicals.
Defensive staples with pricing power benefit from a 3.5% CPI environment and offer relative safety as long-end rates pressure growth multiples.
Cyclical exposure is unattractive when the curve is flattening and the Fed is paused with no near-term easing catalyst.
Consumer-facing strength from low unemployment offsets duration headwinds from the 10y surge; net effect is roughly balanced.
Ad-driven revenue is resilient in a stable labor market, but rising discount rates at 4.69% on the 10y cap upside.
Defensive healthcare benefits from a pause regime with sticky inflation; stable employment supports enrollment volumes.

memos.headline: GOOGL Post-Earnings Selloff Dominates Sentiment; JPM and UNH Tone Turning Positive on Solid Prints
memos.body: I am focused today on the sharp divergence in earnings-driven sentiment across the universe. GOOGL's Q2 results filed 2026-07-22 triggered a -7.1% price reaction through the 7/23 close, the largest single-name move in our coverage and a clear negative narrative shift that may not yet be fully absorbed. In contrast, JPM's 7/14 earnings print drove a +2.5% move and was followed by routine corporate filings through 7/23, suggesting constructive tone with no deterioration—a positive sentiment trajectory I want to lean into. UNH posted a modest +1.2% reaction on its 7/16 results, indicating stable-to-improving tone in a name that has faced headline risk in recent quarters. On the quieter names—AAPL has zero 8-K filings in this window, leaving me with no sentiment signal to act on, while NVDA's filings are all governance-related with no earnings catalyst yet, keeping me neutral until we see a fundamental print.

views.note: A -7.1% post-earnings reaction signals a sharp negative narrative shift that likely has further room to weigh on sentiment in the near term.
Positive +2.5% earnings reaction on 7/14 followed by routine filings suggests constructive tone trajectory with no emerging negatives.
Modest +1.2% earnings reaction on 7/16 indicates stabilizing sentiment, though conviction is limited by the small magnitude of the move.
Only governance and routine filings in the window; no earnings catalyst yet to drive a sentiment view.
Material agreement and other-events filings suggest corporate activity but no earnings print yet to anchor a directional sentiment call.
Large acquisition-related 8-K on 7/1 is notable but without a price reaction or tone data I cannot gauge market sentiment direction.

memos.headline: Oil Spike and Falling Policy Uncertainty Create Divergent Geopolitical Signals Across the Universe
memos.body: I note a sharp 24.7% one-month surge in WTI to $93.08/bbl, which points to a supply-side disruption or geopolitical tension in energy markets, even as the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has collapsed 51% month-over-month to 194—suggesting that whatever drove earlier policy anxiety (likely tariff or sanctions escalation) has materially de-escalated. VIX at 18.70 and HY OAS at 2.77% confirm credit markets are not pricing systemic stress, but the oil move is too large to ignore and creates clear winners (XOM) and losers (CAT, PG via input costs). I have moderate conviction that the oil spike reflects a structural tightening—possibly OPEC+ discipline or Middle East supply risk—rather than a transient event, and I would need to see WTI retreat below $80 or new export-control headlines to change my view on the semiconductor names. NVDA remains the key geopolitical exposure given ongoing China AI-chip restrictions; the June 8-K filing does not clarify any policy relief, so I stay cautious there.

views.note: WTI at $93 with a 25% one-month surge directly benefits upstream earnings; structural supply tightness favors the name until oil retreats below $80.
Policy uncertainty has fallen sharply but no evidence of China export-control relaxation; the June 8-K offers no clarity, so I stay sidelined pending concrete policy signals.
Higher energy costs pressure equipment margins and global infrastructure demand; the June Reg FD disclosure does not offset macro headwinds from $93 oil.
Rising oil lifts petrochemical input costs, but the dramatic drop in policy uncertainty is a tailwind for consumer staples supply chains; net effect is roughly neutral.
Positive yield curve at +34bp and collapsing policy uncertainty support bank earnings; multiple recent 8-Ks suggest active capital-markets activity.
No direct geopolitical catalyst from the evidence; the June Reg FD filing is uninformative on antitrust or China exposure, so I have no edge here.
